title: Decision record
description: One decision a venture has to make, in a decisions/ folder beside the record it decides (EE-054), like a Next.js file beside its route: decisions/<record>[.<topic>].decision.json decides <record>.json in the folder that holds decisions/. The decision log (decision.schema.json) stays the append-only history; this is the live decision. node schema/decisions.mjs gathers them into the decision matrix.

id.description: Unique within the venture. The roots venture and foundation are reserved.

question.description: What has to be decided, as a question

ideas.description: The ideas in the founder's idea dump this decision comes from, by id (purpose/ideas/map.mdx), so a decision can be traced back to the founder's own words (EE-061)

decides.description: What the decision settles: a record type, a venture-relative file, or both. Defaults to the record its file name names.

path.description: A venture-relative file, such as purpose/icp.json

statement.description: The strategic-foundation statement this decision settles (purpose/strategic-foundation.json), if any. It then stands in for that statement in the matrix and is part of the foundation.

layer.description: The layer it belongs to; defaults to the decided record's layer

parent.description: The decision this one depends on. Defaults to foundation for a foundation record, else venture.

boundary.description: fail-closed: while this decision is open, decisions under it wait and agents only draft. fail-open: work under it goes on. inherit: the parent's boundary. The venture root and the foundation fail closed; a product fails open (EE-054).

needed_in.description: The phase in which it must be made. One needed in a later phase than the venture's is speculative and held back (EE-057).

due.description: When it must be decided, for a decision with a real deadline (a launch, a hackathon, a filing). An open decision past its due time renders overdue; a due time overrides needed_in, so a dated decision is never held back as later.

decided_by.description: Who decided: a person's name. An agent never decides a fail-closed decision. Deprecated in favour of provenance.approved_by, which it must equal when both are present.

logged_as.description: The decision log entry that records it, such as D-012 or EE-054

provenance.description: Who worded and who approved the decision, when, and in which phase (EE-058). An agent's wording waits with drafted_by alone; a decided decision needs approved_by, approved_at and phase.

kind.description: framework: Naive asked the question itself, as a convention (the product foundation); a person still answers it

id.description: The person's name or the agent's id

approved_by.description: The person who approved the wording or changed it. Never an agent.

phase.description: The venture's phase when it was approved

wording.description: approved: the drafted wording as it was; changed: the approver altered it; own: the approver wrote it

authority.description: The decision class in governance/decision-rights.json under which the approver could decide, when authority was delegated

via.description: Where the approval was given, such as the Decision Docket or a decision card

outcomes.description: What the decision is expected to achieve, and later what happened; the evaluations it is tested against (EE-058). Outcomes, not activities.

by.description: When it should be visible: a date-time, a date or a phase. A pending outcome past a date-time or date is due for its actual result.

unlocks.description: Activities this decision opens that were closed before it (EE-058), and for whom

for.description: Roles, people or agents it opens for; empty means everyone

routes.description: The routes the activity uses, as globs such as operations/** (robots syntax). Until the decision is made, the router refuses agents those routes (for the actors in for, or every agent).
